_comment: Declared BEFORE the first run. Do not loosen a target to make a run pass; change it only with a written reason and a date in notes. Every number in the Cooky docs lives here; prose points at these keys.

notes.min_receipt_auto_accept_precision: Share of receipt lines Cooky auto-accepts (not flagged) whose ingredient, quantity and unit are all correct. This is the CORE TENSION, side one: a wrong item that slips in silently corrupts every plan and alert built on the fridge. One silent error per twenty lines is the most a user forgives before they stop trusting the fridge.
notes.max_receipt_flag_rate: Share of food lines flagged for the user to check. CORE TENSION, side two: if more than about one line in three needs attention, logging feels like typing it in by hand, which is the chore that killed earlier fridge apps. Measured together with min_receipt_auto_accept_precision on the same receipts; neither may be bought by trading the other.
notes.min_receipt_food_line_recall: Share of food lines on the receipt that appear in the draft at all (auto or flagged). A dropped line is an item the fridge will never know about.
notes.max_receipt_log_time_p50_s: Median seconds from tapping 'scan receipt' to a confirmed fridge update, measured by stopwatch in the pilot. About the time it takes to put groceries away; typing a typical trip by hand takes several minutes. v1: measured in the classmate test.
notes.min_recipe_import_ingredient_accuracy: Share of ingredient rows in an imported draft with the right catalog ingredient, quantity and unit. Below this, users must fix most imports by hand and stop importing.
notes.min_shopping_calc_exact_rate: Shopping math is deterministic code. Package counts, cents and leftovers must match the hand-computed answers exactly; any miss is a bug, not a tolerance.
notes.min_plan_constraint_pass_rate: Share of shown plans with zero violations: no excluded or allergen ingredient, no duplicate meal, no unknown id, total within budget. Enforced in code, so anything below 1.0 means the guardrail is broken.
notes.min_plan_success_rate: Share of plan requests that have at least one feasible set and end in a valid plan within the repair cap. The rest must fail honestly with an error, never a fake plan.
notes.min_infeasible_honesty_rate: When no feasible set exists, the share of runs that say so (with the cheapest feasible estimate or hints) instead of showing a plan.
notes.min_cook_retrieval_recall_at_k: Retrieval stage of the cooking assistant: share of reference questions whose expected step or FAQ id is in the retrieved set. Measured separately from generation so a bad answer can be traced to its stage.
notes.min_cook_citation_valid_rate: Every citation id in an answer must be one retrieved in that same run. Enforced in code, so anything below 1.0 is a guardrail bug.
notes.min_cook_answer_faithfulness: Generation stage: share of answers whose claims all follow from the cited chunks, labelled by a person. A cooking assistant that invents steps ruins dinners.
notes.min_evidence_gap_honesty_rate: Share of out-of-recipe or unsupported questions answered with 'not covered by this recipe' or a clarifying question, instead of a confident guess.
notes.min_fridge_consistency_rate: After the scripted journey (receipt confirm, cook confirm, toss, fridge check, retries and double-clicks), the share of fridge items whose quantity equals the ledger's expected value. The fridge is the product; it must not drift.
notes.min_expiry_alert_recall: Every active item whose expiry falls inside the alert lead window gets an alert from the next daily run. Pure code, so it must be complete.
notes.min_guardrail_block_rate: Share of bad cases stopped: prompt injection in receipts and imported pages, another user's ids, unpaid calls to Pro routes, SSRF import URLs, over-quota calls.
notes.max_guardrail_false_block_rate: Share of normal requests in the guardrail set that are wrongly blocked. A guardrail that blocks good users is as broken as one that lets bad requests through.
notes.min_billing_scenario_pass_rate: The eight billing scenarios (success, cancel, failed card, duplicate webhook, bad signature, delayed webhook, unpaid Pro call, already-Pro checkout) must all pass. Money is never approximately right.
notes.max_plan_p95_ms: A plan is a deliberate action with a progress screen; past this, users assume it is stuck. Includes the agent's tool calls and repairs.
notes.max_receipt_parse_p95_ms: The user is standing in the kitchen holding the receipt; past this they put the phone down. Parsing is synchronous in v1, so this also guards the serverless function timeout.
notes.max_recipe_import_p95_ms: Same tolerance as receipt parsing: one deliberate wait with a progress indicator.
notes.max_cook_answer_p95_ms: Asked mid-cooking with hands busy; an answer slower than this arrives after the pan burns.
notes.max_api_read_p95_ms: Non-AI reads (fridge, recipes, plans) are the cheap path and must feel instant.
notes.max_error_rate_pct: Share of requests ending in an unexpected 5xx across the benchmark. Honest, expected errors (422 infeasible, 429 quota) do not count.
notes.max_cost_per_plan_usd: One planner call plus at most the allowed repairs, priced at costModel rates. Changed 2026-10-20, before any run: default model moved to claude-haiku-5-5 for the team's small budget; value set from Haiku prices with headroom.
notes.max_cost_per_receipt_usd: One vision call plus at most one repair, catalog in a cached prefix. Leaves room to step this unit up to claude-sonnet-5-5 if Haiku misses its smoke targets. Changed 2026-10-20, before any run: default model moved to claude-haiku-5-5 for the team's small budget; value set from Haiku prices with headroom.
notes.max_cost_per_import_usd: One extraction call plus at most one repair over a page snapshot capped by limits.importTextMaxChars (v2 feature). Changed 2026-10-20, before any run: default model moved to claude-haiku-5-5 for the team's small budget; value set from Haiku prices with headroom.
notes.max_cost_per_cook_answer_usd: The highest-volume AI feature; a cooking session can ask many questions. Changed 2026-10-20, before any run: default model moved to claude-haiku-5-5 for the team's small budget; value set from Haiku prices with headroom.
notes.min_overbuy_reduction_pct: Pilot comparison, exploratory: the same week of meals planned by hand vs. with Cooky, counting units bought beyond what the recipes need after subtracting what was already at home. Small sample; reported honestly even if missed. Measured in v2 only (week-long pilot); v1 runs a short classmate test and reports it qualitatively.
notes.min_planning_time_reduction_pct: Pilot comparison, exploratory: minutes from 'what should I cook this week' to a finished shopping list, by hand vs. with Cooky. Measured in v2 only (week-long pilot); v1 runs a short classmate test and reports it qualitatively.

quotas._comment: Per user. Enforced atomically in src/platform/quotas.ts before any model call. Free = lifetime counts; pro = per calendar day in the user's timezone.

costModel.source: Anthropic first-party API rates, claude-api skill model table (cached 2026-10-06). Re-check on the pricing page before the write-up.
costModel.note: Default changed from claude-opus-5-5 to claude-haiku-5-5 on 2026-10-20 at the team's request (small budget; a simple model is enough). Haiku prices apply to prompts up to 100K tokens.

receipts.note: Real receipts from team members, card digits and loyalty numbers blurred before commit.

imports.note: Saved page snapshots, not live URLs, so anchors do not move.

smokeSets._comment: v1 (demo day). Enough to catch breakage and show good and failed examples; not a statistical claim.

measuredIn._comment: Which targets the v1 gate checks. Everything else is reported if measured, and becomes blocking in v2.
